newsitem.title: PANAMA: BellSouth extends Panama's cellular service.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth extends Panama's cellular service.

text.p: A consortium led by U.S. telecommunications company BellSouth Corp expanded cellular phone service to Panama's second largest city, a company spokeswoman said Tuesday.
"As of today, cellular phone service is working in Colon and along the highway from Panama City to Colon," said the spokeswoman.
Colon is located on the Atlantic coast 50 miles (80 km) from Panama City.
The company is working on establishing a roaming service with the United States and Venezuela by the end of the year or the beginning of 1997, she said.
The roaming service would allow customers to use their cellular phones purchased in Panama in those countries, she said.
BSC de Panama SA, a consortium headed by BellSouth, won the license to build and operate Panama's first cellular telephone network in January with a bid of $72.61 million.

BellSouth, operator of the BSC consortium, has the largest stake with 41.5 percent. Other investors are Panama's Multi Holding Corp, a holding company of Grupo Bancomer de Panama and Guatemala's Grupo Botran.

The consortium received a 20-year license to operate Band A, one of two nationwide cellular telephone bands. The other band will be operated by state-run telephone company INTEL, currently undergoing a partial privatization process.
